newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end sharply lower in all months.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end sharply lower in all months.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed sharply lower in all months on Thursday, reflecting declines in the Chicago corn market overnight, traders said.
Prices were 340 to 470 yen lower, with the benchmark July 1998 contract down 470 yen at 13,990 yen per tonne.
The day's estimated volume was 58,777 lots.
Active selling emerged throughout the day, particularly in the distant months, traders said. "Some powerful investors actively liquidated long positions," a brokerage house trader said.
Traders said they are watching to see whether the benchmark July 1998 contract will fall further below the 14,000 yen level.
The spot July corn contract on the CBOT Project A overnight trading system stood at $2.66-1/4 per bushel at 0740 GMT, against $2.66-1/2 at Wednesday's close.
Spot July CBOT soybean futures were trading at $8.31-1/2 a bushel at 0740 GMT, against $8.32-1/2 at Wednesday's close.
